lines.text: When dinosaurs were alive, a day wasn't twenty-four hours.
lines.caption: When dinosaurs were alive, a day wasn't 24 hours.

lines.text: It was shorter. And that's not even the weird part.
Seventy million years ago, Earth spun faster. A day lasted about twenty-three and a half hours.
lines.caption: 70 million years ago, Earth spun faster. A day lasted about 23.5 hours.

lines.text: Scientists read it in a fossil clam, which grew a new layer every single day, like tree rings.
The culprit is the Moon. Its tides work like a brake, slowing Earth down, a tiny bit every century.
And the weird part? Back then, one year had three hundred and seventy-two days.
lines.caption: And the weird part? Back then, one year had 372 days.
